packageRules.description: Angular majors go through the update-angular skill: ng update's migrations across the packages and ~100 examples, the published peer ranges, and the docs, none of which a version bump does. Minors and patches still come through.

Architect is versioned 0.MMmm.p (Angular 22.2 is 0.2202), so semver calls its move to the next Angular major (0.2300) a minor, and the rule above doesn't catch it. The update-angular skill moves this bound up with each major.
Each Angular release accepts only some TypeScript minors (its typescript peer range), so a TypeScript minor on its own fails the install. The update-angular skill moves TypeScript with Angular.

@types/node's major is the Node version it types, and the packages support Node 22.12 and later (engines), so a newer major lets the type check pass code using an API Node 22 lacks. Majors move by hand.

The examples and packages/ui use Tailwind 3 on purpose: @lynx-js/tailwind-preset supports only Tailwind 3 (peer ^3.4.0), and with Tailwind 4 the build skips their tailwind.config.ts and they render unstyled though the build passes. examples/tailwind-4 covers Tailwind 4. Majors move by hand.

The rsbuild plugin hands rspack plugins a Compiler from @lynx-js/rspeedy, which pins an exact @rsbuild/core and so an @rspack/core minor (2.2 in rspeedy 0.18.6). The plugin types that Compiler with its own @rspack/core, so a newer minor installs a second copy and its declaration build fails on the two Compiler types (#506). Move it by hand when rspeedy moves. @rsbuild/core minors build fine (#505).
Each @ng-native package peers on the others at its exact version, so one moved alone fails the install (ERESOLVE). They move together.

The angular-lynx benchmark installs @blotch/* from tarballs that scripts/use-local-packages.mjs packs into .local-packages/, which is git-ignored, so Renovate never has them and every lockfile update there fails (#509). Its versions move by hand: copy the bumped entries from the root lockfile, or rerun the script after a root build.

The React Native benchmark apps keep their versions on purpose. apps/react-native is Software Mansion's app on the exact versions its original lockfile resolved, and apps/react-native-0.88 is that app moved to Expo SDK 58 with `npx expo install --fix`, which sets React Native and its libraries to the versions the SDK pins together: SDK 58 takes react-native-reanimated 4.7.1 with react-native-worklets 0.13.0, so 4.8.0 on its own fails the install (#566). CI doesn't build either app, so a bump's checks pass even when the app no longer installs. They move by redoing the Expo upgrade, as apps/react-native-0.88/README.md describes.

The angular-native benchmark is an Expo SDK 58 app too, and its React Native side is the set the SDK pins: react 19.3.0, react-native 0.88.1 and react-native-svg 15.16.0 exactly, with the expo modules and the other native libraries on their SDK 58 lines. It's measured against apps/react-native-0.88, which the rule above holds still, so a bump here alone (#582, #583) would compare library versions as well as frameworks. These move with that app, by redoing the Expo upgrade (`npx expo install --fix`). Angular, @ng-native and the app's other dependencies still come through.

The Android template gets Lynx and PrimJS from Maven, but iOS gets them from our own XCFrameworks zip (packages/native/src/ios/frameworks.ts), which the Lynx iOS frameworks workflow builds and Renovate can't. An update on Android alone would put the two platforms on different Lynx versions, and 4.1.2 added list item animations (#590). So Lynx updates wait on the Dependency Dashboard: tick one to get the Android half, build the iOS zip for the same version as packages/native/README.md describes, and move both in that PR.
